messages:
mike_infra: Heads up — seeing p95 east-west latency spikes between gpunode-* during the 10:30-11:00 batch window in us-west-2. Started ~10:35, looks correlated with the NIC offload toggle rollout. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abcd123/batch-latency. Oncall alerted.
infra-bot: [ALERT] east-west-p95>250ms us-west-2 batch-window - triggered at 2026-03-18T10:35:12Z

sarah_sre: Can you paste the exact graph and packet loss numbers? Any retransmits or checksum errors? What change was rolled out?

mike_infra: Quick numbers: p50 ~4ms, p95 jumped to 320-480ms, packet loss ~0.8-1.2% between rack-A <-> rack-B (ixgbe0). Spike aligns with sustained batches >2048 tokens. Change: flip `disable-gso=false` via rollout at 10:32.

jess_ml: Sounds like an offload/coalescing mismatch (GRO/GSO/LRO + HW checksums) causing extra fanout/queueing on the path. Can you run `ethtool -k` / `ethtool -i` and `tc -s qdisc` on both sides of an affected link? Also capture a short pcap between two affected GPUs.

mike_infra: Running checks now, snippets below.

```bash
# ethtool -k ixgbe0
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
tcp6-segmentation-offload: off
generic-segmentation-offload: on
generic-receive-offload: off

# tc -s qdisc show dev ixgbe0
qdisc mq 0: root rate 0x
 qlen 1000
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
```

mike_infra: Also ran tcpdump for a 60s window on src/dst pair: `sudo tcpdump -i ixgbe0 -w /tmp/eastwest.pcap 'tcp and host 10.0.12.34 and host 10.0.56.78'`. Observed repeated retransmit bursts aligned to batching start and many small frames (possible GSO split).

tomas_devx: Can we quick rollback the NIC offload flag? If it's the only obvious change, revert and see if p95 normalizes. Also, consider routing traffic over alternate spine for the peak window.

mike_infra: Rolled back NIC Offload change via ansible to 6 hosts in the path: `ansible-playbook playbooks/rollback-nic-offload.yml --limit gpunode-12,gpunode-13,gpunode-14,gpunode-15,gpunode-16,gpunode-17`. Results: 4/6 completed successfully (2 reboots pending). After revert the 4 hosts show p95 ~28ms. Cluster-wide p95 improved from ~420ms to ~120ms.

sarah_sre: Great. For the two still pending, verify firmware/driver versions — we've seen checksum fallback cause extra CPU path handling. Run `ethtool -i ixgbe0` and compare `driver` + `firmware-version`.

mike_infra: Checked: the 2 pending had older firmware (ixgbe 5.6.1 vs 5.9.0). Filed INF-3421 to upgrade firmware and finish the rollback.

jess_ml: For long-term: add a canary policy for NIC config changes (small percentage of nodes + perf harness that runs intra-node microbenchmarks during rollout). Also add a rule: if intra-cluster p95 >200ms during a rollout window, auto-pause the rollout and pin batch size to safe default.

tomas_devx: I created a short runbook and a tmp doc: runbook/infra/eastwest-burst-fanout.md (internal). Owners: @mike_infra for rollback + verification, @sarah_sre for alert thresholds, @jess_ml for rollout policy changes.

mike_infra: PCAP and artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/pcaps/1976543210-eastwest.pcap.gz and s3://redwood-artifacts/logs/1976543210-rollback.log. I'll add a timeline to the ticket.

sarah_sre: Scheduling a postmortem tomorrow 09:30 PT to capture root cause and action items. Tagging @all FYI. :calendar: :memo:

ops-oncall: Incident marked sev2 -> mitigated (partial rollback reduced impact). Keeping it open until postmortem and firmware upgrades complete.

mike_infra: Thanks — will follow up with remediation steps and a test plan for NIC toggles. :thumbsup:
